content.value_statement: Large codebases collect dead code, duplicate logic, and unclear boundaries over time. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a structured architecture audit.
actual_capabilities: Maps project structure and identifies source entry points.
Checks exports, imports, and usage patterns to find dead code.
Catalogs duplicate logic, duplicate types, and overlapping utilities.
Flags architecture issues such as large files, cycles, coupling, and layer violations.
Reviews type abuse, complex code, magic values, naming issues, and commented code.
Produces a structured Markdown report with impact estimates and cleanup priorities.
limitations: It depends on local repository access and search tools such as find and grep.
Dynamic imports, reflection, framework conventions, and public APIs may need manual verification.
It reports findings only and explicitly instructs the agent not to edit project files.
Large repositories may require careful progress tracking to avoid incomplete coverage.

use_cases.title: Prepare A Refactor Plan
use_cases.description: Identify dead code, duplicate modules, and architecture risks before assigning cleanup work.

use_cases.title: Review A Legacy Codebase
use_cases.description: Map structural problems and estimate cleanup impact before changing inherited code.

use_cases.title: Improve TypeScript Health
use_cases.description: Find unsafe type usage, duplicate interfaces, and code smells that reduce maintainability.

prompt_templates.title: Run A Basic Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit of a small project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the architectural-analysis skill to review this repository. Focus on dead code, duplicate logic, and the highest impact cleanup opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Audit TypeScript Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the architectural-analysis skill on this TypeScript project. Prioritize type confusion, unsafe any usage, duplicate types, and module boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Find Refactor Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the architectural-analysis skill to find refactor candidates. Rank dead files, duplicate utilities, large modules, cycles, and layer violations by impact.

prompt_templates.title: Produce An Executive Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the architectural-analysis skill for a full repository audit. Create the report, quantify cleanup potential, and separate confirmed issues from items needing verification.

output_examples.input: Review a TypeScript service before a refactor.
output_examples.output: A Markdown audit listing dead files, unused exports, duplicate utilities, architecture issues, and cleanup estimates.

output_examples.input: Assess a legacy frontend for maintainability risks.
output_examples.output: A prioritized report covering large components, layer violations, unsafe type usage, repeated logic, and suggested ownership areas.

output_examples.input: Prepare cleanup work for a sprint planning meeting.
output_examples.output: A concise summary with top dead files, duplicate groups, architectural risks, and verification notes for uncertain findings.

best_practices: Run the audit from the repository root so path searches cover the full project.
Verify possible dead code against dynamic imports, framework hooks, and public API contracts.
Use the generated report as a planning artifact before making cleanup changes.
anti_patterns: Do not delete files directly from the audit results without manual verification.
Do not treat similar names as duplication until the underlying logic is compared.
Do not skip tests, generated boundaries, or entry points when deciding whether code is unused.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my code?
faq.answer: No. The instructions explicitly require analysis only and prohibit editing files during the audit.

faq.question: Which languages does it fit best?
faq.answer: It is written around TypeScript and JavaScript examples, but the audit method can guide other source trees.

faq.question: Can it find all dead code automatically?
faq.answer: No. Dynamic imports, reflection, framework hooks, and public APIs can require manual confirmation.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a Markdown report with dead code, duplication, architecture issues, type issues, code smells, and impact estimates.

faq.question: Why does it use shell examples?
faq.answer: The examples show local search commands for repository discovery and usage checks. They are not installation or network commands.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
